Title: Yielded title and vampire entering play

Messages.Author: dea...@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
I need a clarification for these three situations. In all of them,
there has been a contest for titles between Vampire A and Vampire B.
Vampire A has yielded his title. Vampire B is still in play.

1) Vampire A was Banished, then returned to play. Does contest start
anew?

2) Vampire A was burned, then another copy of him entered play. Does
contest start anew?

3) Vampire A was Banished, then another copy of him entered play.
Does contest start anew?

(The only relevant bit of information I've found is this ruling:

A Banished vampire will remember all effects that had been applied to
him, just as contested vampires do. This includes gained or lost
titles, etc. [RTR 20000501]

It suggests the answer "No" to the first question. It seems that the
answer to the last two questions is "Yes", in lack of any reason for
it to be otherwise.)

Thanks,
Arry

Messages.Author: Jozxyqk
Messages.Body:
dea...@gmail.com wrote:
> I need a clarification for these three situations. In all of them,
> there has been a contest for titles between Vampire A and Vampire B.
> Vampire A has yielded his title. Vampire B is still in play.

> 1) Vampire A was Banished, then returned to play. Does contest start
> anew?

No.

> 2) Vampire A was burned, then another copy of him entered play. Does
> contest start anew?

Yes. Even if Vampire A was burned and then Possessed from the ash heap,
he would come into play with his printed title.

> 3) Vampire A was Banished, then another copy of him entered play.
> Does contest start anew?

This one is tricky. Since the uncontrolled region is unordered and
can be "shuffled", there's no way to prove that a vampire who took a
trip into the uncontrolled region is different from another uncontrolled
copy of him.
I would say:
If the banished copy had cards/counters on him that distinguish him from
another facedown version of the same vampire, and you bring out the "other"
one, then "Yes".
But if the other copy is identical-in-every-way in the uncontrolled region,
then you have no way to prove he is different, so "No".

So let's say that this is the situation:
I have Gilbert Duane in play, who has yielded his title, and has zero blood.
I also have Gilbert Duane (Gil Prime) in my uncontrolled region, who has never
entered play.

Gilbert Duane gets banished (by Imogen).
I shuffle my crypt because it's legal to do so.
Then, later on in the game, a vampire named Gilbert Duane enters play from
my uncontrolled region. It may be Gilbert Duane, it may be Gil Prime, or
it may be even a third copy of Gilbert who is Red List and has also
been banished empty (Gilbert the Red).
Of course it's to my advantage to "fiat" it to be Gil Prime. But it's to
Imogen's controller's advantage to "fiat" it to be Gilbert Duane. And it's
to Norm's advantage to "fiat" it to be Gilbert the Red.

How is this distinction made fairly?

If Gil Prime was Jyhad-backed and Gilbert Duane was VTES-backed, is that
relevant to the distinction (assuming an unsleeved crypt)?

Does it _require_ you to mark uncontrolled vampires with non-counter/non-
card effects on them to distinguish them between each other?

Frankly, I think this whole set of corner-case situations would be cleaner
if "reordering" the uncontrolled region were illegal.
But it's up to the Rules Team to determine whether this is worth putting up
for review or not, I guess...
